body.statement: Run \(\mathfrak C\) on the complete rational input \(\Xi_0\) in \(\mathrm{def{:}fixed\text{-}protocol}\). If and only if its status is \(\mathtt{UNDECIDED}\), run it once more on the uniquely prescribed replacement \(\Xi_1=\mathfrak F_0(\Xi_0)\); do not refine after \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\) or \(\mathtt{REFUTED}\). Does one of these two runs return \(\mathtt{CERTIFIED}\), thereby proving positive nonvacuous wrong-graph, Jacobian, remote-identification, and local-injectivity bounds, valid tails, and \(N_{\mathrm{req}}\leq200000\) for the synthetic \(p=3\), \((i_X,i_Y,i_Z)=(1,2,3)\) benchmark?
body.justification: This is a falsifiable application of the reusable procedure, not the headline theorem and not evidence for an existing biological assay.
body.gap: The floating-point pilot checks only two local witness Jacobians and no wrong-graph boxes; it does not establish any uniform premise used by the inference theorem.
body.consumer: A certified answer licenses only the stated synthetic prospective benchmark; a collision, singularity, or precision obstruction stops that protocol without affecting the rank frontier.
